title: Tenant-visible 5xx oscillation and idempotency guard implementation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported intermittent 5xx spikes and prolonged timeouts during tenant surges. Investigation showed an interaction between the edge retry policy, backend batching heuristics, and KV cache eviction that caused oscillating inflight requests leading to overloaded worker queues. This ticket tracks the targeted bugfixes, mitigations, and customer comms for Hosted (primary), with notes for Dedicated and Private deployment variants.
comments: 2025-02-12 09:10 - Asha Patel: Alert from oncall: tenant T-842 experienced 5xx burst at ~08:45 UTC correlating with a large fanout of short streaming requests. Slack #incidents thread created. Initial triage points to increased inflight requests and elevated worker latencies.

2025-02-12 10:30 - Diego Morales: Captured flamegraphs and queue length metrics. Observed repeated request replays from edge layer because client retries + proxy retries + backend hedging created amplification. Noticed KV cache compaction running concurrently, which increased cold-start latency for affected model shards.

2025-02-12 12:05 - Sofia Chen (SRE): Rolled soft throttle for the tenant at the edge (connection-hold) to reduce immediate pressure; customer notified via ticket with temporary mitigation. Added tenant-shaped leaky bucket with 500ms backoff between attempts.

2025-02-12 16:40 - Diego Morales: Reproduced locally using synthetic load: sequence of many short, single-token streaming calls triggers a kernel path that allocates per-request resources and serializes to the same GPU host. Queue length grows non-linearly when retries are honored downstream. Created reproduction script and uploaded to Drive: https://drive.redwood/repro/ENG-202315.

2025-02-13 08:20 - Asha Patel: Drafted rollback-safe mitigation: (1) align edge retry windows with backend idempotency token check, (2) add admission control at proxy for tenant-scoped concurrent requests, (3) add temporary KV cache compaction hold during surges. Preparing PRs.

2025-02-13 14:15 - Diego Morales: Opened PR GH-11234: 'edge: honor idempotency tokens and short-circuit duplicate inflight' — implements idempotency token dedup table with TTL and metrics. Benchmarked; decreases duplicate backend calls by ~78% in repro.

2025-02-14 09:00 - Sofia Chen: Deployed canary of GH-11234 to us-east-1 edge pool for 10 customers including T-842. Observed immediate reduction of repeat calls; 5xx rate for canary tenants dropped from 6.1% to 1.4% in first 2h. No negative impact on latency observed.

2025-02-15 11:50 - Customer Success (Lena Morris): Communicated interim mitigation and ETA for full fix to impacted customers. Collected additional logs from Dedicated customer C-390 (different infra) — their stack shows fewer retries but similar queue saturation symptom due to worker scheduling.

2025-02-16 10:05 - Diego Morales: Minor follow-up patch GH-11301: 'runtime: avoid compaction-trigger during inflight surge' — defers KV compaction when eviction pressure and queue depth both exceed thresholds. Canary results good; memory impact minimal.

2025-02-17 15:30 - Asha Patel: Drafted post-incident runbook updates and added an automatic circuit-breaker config for tenant surges. Runbook added to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/tenant-surge-runbook. Need PM sign-off on communications template.

2025-02-18 09:45 - Diego Morales: Remaining work: extend idempotency guard to Private (on-prem) runtime (requires config toggle for local KVS), add metric dashboards for 'idempotent-duplicates' and tenant-level inflight headroom, and schedule targeted load test for Dedicated clusters. Assigned follow-ups as subtasks.

2025-02-18 12:00 - Asha Patel: Noted: updated_at bumped after coordination call with PM and SRE. Preparing for wider rollout to hosted edge fleet tomorrow morning if no regressions seen in next 24h Canary window.
resolution_summary: Deployed multi-layer mitigation: (1) edge-level idempotency dedup reduces duplicate in-flight backend calls, (2) admission control prevents tenant burst fanout from filling worker queues, (3) deferred KV compaction during surge avoids added latency. Canary telemetry shows significant drop in 5xx rates for affected tenants. Next: roll out to remaining regions and backport config toggles for Dedicated/Private customers.
notes_for_dedicated_private: Dedicated: recommend applying idempotency guard at edge proxy in front of reserved pools and enable tenant-scoped admission control in Dedicated autoscaler; will require a minor config change in dedicated-config v2 to expose per-tenant concurrency caps.
Private/on-prem: provide a deployable toggle and migration docs — some customers run air-gapped KVS; we will ship an in-memory fallback with operator guidance for safe TTL sizing.
